core.text: The observed synthetic miswrite is refresh followed by retained-row commit. Recurrence remains unobserved. Hypothesis: its mismatch requests a further refresh, and delivery while another row selection is retained can cause a second miswrite. Intervene specifically on mismatch-triggered refresh delivery, keeping target demand K2/K5/K7 and ordinary refreshes fixed.

Propose matched scripted diagnostic arms starting from S0: select K2 during 0-1; ordinary refresh during 1-2; commit during 2-3; select intended K5 at S1 row 2 during 3-4. At the return gate during 4-5, deliver the initial mismatch-triggered refresh in one arm; suppress it in the other and inspect the intended key for one minute without changing selection. Commit during 5-6 and perform the same final refresh during 6-7. This preserves elapsed time and snapshot eligibility while changing the return link.

Prospective stipulated-model prediction: both arms initially write K5 instead of K2. Return delivery then loads S2, so the second commit writes K7 instead of intended K5; suppression retains S1 and writes intended K5. Record the request, delivery, loaded snapshot, retained row, intended key and actual key. Under frozen S0 or immutable-key binding, the same return delivery should not produce this additional wrong-target write. These controls localize the proposed mechanism to reorder plus row binding.

residue.text: These are causal diagnostics, not successful correction traces: both already violate the prohibition on any incorrect-key write. The valued outcome still requires exactly K2/K5/K7 checked, five unchecked, read-only scores, latest snapshot and completion within ten minutes. Final correctness cannot erase earlier miswrites.

K5 and K7 share score 75 in S2; compare immutable keys, not scores. Neither repeated feedback nor the proposed return-gate timing is supplied as observed. A diagnostic contrast would establish a synthetic causal possibility under scripted delivery, not actual recurrence, real editor binding, detection reliability, operational savings or human benefit.

tension.account_a: Causal return account: a mismatch-triggered refresh can generate a subsequent wrong-key write by reordering a retained row selection.
tension.account_b: Symptom-only account: mismatch-triggered refresh requests have no causal effect on subsequent wrong-key writes; ordinary refreshes alone explain them.
tension.prediction_a: At the matched return gate, delivery predicts second actual key K7 and suppression predicts K5; the contrast disappears with frozen ordering or immutable-key binding.
tension.prediction_b: At the matched return gate, delivery and suppression predict identical second written keys and wrong-write counts. A verified K7-versus-K5 contrast contradicts this account.
